title: SentenceLDA: Discriminative and Robust Document Representation with Sentence Level Topic Model
problem: Word-level topic models rely on spelling, so lexically similar documents with different topics are confused and paraphrases are not recognised.
architecture: Gaussian LDA where the observed unit is a SentenceBERT sentence embedding: topics are Gaussians (Normal-Inverse-Wishart priors) in embedding space, each sentence draws a topic from the document's Dirichlet topic proportions; Gibbs sampling; topic sentences decoded for interpretation.

datasets.name: 20News
datasets.details: 18,846 documents (18,327 non-empty), 6 coarse and 20 fine classes

metrics: classification accuracy and F1 (logistic regression, random forest)
key_results: 20News, 20 topics, all classes: accuracy 42.73% vs SenClu 40.91% and LDA 37.99%.
NYT, 20 topics, all classes: LDA is better (82.98% vs 65.65%).
strengths: Keeps LDA's probabilistic interpretation while working at sentence level.
Explicit robustness test with paraphrased texts.

limitations.text: Very slow: 20 sampling iterations on NYT with 20 topics take nearly a day; coherence/diversity metrics for sentence-level topics are lacking; generated topic sentences may be non-factual.
Word-level LDA beats SentenceLDA on several NYT settings (e.g. all 26 classes, sports).

notes: SenClu trained on merged train/test data, which may favour it.
